{{Short description|Mathematical concept in algebraic topology}}
In [[mathematics]], particularly in [[algebraic topology]], a '''taut pair''' is a [[topological pair]] <math>(A,B)</math>, whose [[cohomology]] modules <math> H^{q}(A,B;G)</math> are isomorphic to the [[direct limit]] of the cohomology modules <math> H^{q}(U,V;G),</math> with <math>(U,V)</math> a pair of open neighborhoods of <math>(A,B)</math>, where the direct limit is induced by inclusion.

==Definition==
For a topological pair <math>(A,B)</math> in a topological space <math>X</math>, a ''neighborhood'' <math>(U,V)</math> of such a pair is defined to be a pair such that <math>U</math> and <math>V</math> are [[neighborhood (mathematics)|neighborhoods]] of <math>A</math> and <math>B</math> respectively.

If we collect all neighborhoods of <math>(A,B)</math>, then we can form a [[directed set]] which is directed downward by inclusion. Hence its cohomology module <math>H^q(U,V;G)</math> is a direct system where <math>G</math> is a module over a ring with unity. If we denote its direct limit by
:<math>\bar{H}^q(A,B;G)=\varinjlim H^q(U,V;G)</math>
the [[Restriction (mathematics)|restriction maps]] <math>H^q(U,V;G)\to H^q(A,B;G)</math> define a natural homomorphism <math>i:\bar{H}^q(A,B;G)\to H^q(A,B;G)</math>.

The pair <math>(A,B)</math> is said to be ''tautly embedded'' in <math>X</math> (or a ''taut pair'' in <math>X</math>) if <math>i</math> is an isomorphism for all <math>q</math> and <math>G</math>.<ref name="auto">{{cite book |last1=Spanier |first1=Edwin H. |title=Algebraic topology |date=1966 |page=289|publisher=Springer |isbn=978-0387944265}}</ref>

==Basic properties==
* For pair <math>(A,B)</math> of <math>X</math>, if two of the three pairs <math>(B,\emptyset),(A,\emptyset)</math>, and <math>(A,B)</math> are taut in <math>X</math>, so is the third.
* For pair <math>(A,B)</math> of <math>X</math>, if <math>A,B</math> and <math>X</math> have [[compact (mathematics)|compact]] [[triangulation]], then <math>(A,B)</math> in <math>X</math> is taut.
* If <math>U</math> varies over the neighborhoods of <math>A</math>, there is an isomorphism <math>\varinjlim \bar{H}^q(U;G)\simeq \bar{H}^q(A;G)</math>.
* If <math>(A,B)</math> and <math>(A',B')</math> are closed pairs in a normal space <math>X</math>, there is an exact relative [[Mayer-Vietoris sequence]] for any coefficient module <math>G</math><ref>{{cite book |last1=Spanier |first1=Edwin H. |title=Algebraic topology |date=1966 |page=290-291|publisher=Springer |isbn=978-0387944265}}</ref>
:<math>\cdots\to\bar{H}^q(A\cup A',B\cup B')\to\bar{H}^q(A,B)\oplus\bar{H}^q(A',B')\to \bar{H}^q(A\cap A',B\cap B')\to\cdots</math>

==Properties related to cohomology theory==
* Let <math>A</math> be any subspace of a topological space <math>X</math> which is a [[Retraction (topology)|neighborhood retract]] of <math>X</math>. Then <math>A</math> is a taut subspace of <math>X</math> with respect to [[Alexander-Spanier cohomology]].
*every retract of an arbitrary [[topological space]] is a taut subspace of <math>X</math> with respect to Alexander-Spanier cohomology.
* A closed subspace of a paracompactt [[Hausdorff space]] is a taut subspace of relative to the Alexander cohomology theory<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Deo |first1=Satya |title=On the tautness property of Alexander-Spanier cohomology |journal=  Proceedings of the American Mathematical Society|date=197 |volume=52 |issue=1 |pages=441–444 |doi=10.2307/2040179|jstor=2040179 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

===Note===
Since the [[Čech cohomology]] and the Alexander-Spanier cohomology are naturally isomorphic on the category of all topological pairs,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dowker |first1=C. H. |title=Homology groups of relations |journal=Annals of Mathematics |date=1952 |volume=(2) 56 |issue=1 |pages=84–95 |doi=10.2307/1969768 |jstor=1969768 }}</ref> all of the above properties are valid for Čech cohomology. However, it's not true for singular cohomology (''see Example'')

==Dependence of cohomology theory==
===Example===
Source:<ref>{{cite book |last1=Spanier |first1=Edwin H. |title=Algebraic topology |date=1966 |page=317|publisher=Springer |isbn=978-0387944265}}</ref>

Let <math>X</math> be the subspace of <math>\mathbb R^2\subset S^2</math> which is the union of four sets
:<math>A_1 = \{(x,y)\mid x =0,-2\leq y\leq 1\}</math>
:<math>A_2 = \{(x,y)\mid 0\leq x\leq 1,y =-2\}</math>
:<math>A_3 = \{(x,y)\mid x = 1,-2\leq y\leq 0\}</math>
:<math>A_4 =\{(x,y)\mid 0<x\leq 1,y =\sin 2\pi/x\}</math>
The first singular cohomology of <math>X</math> is <math>H^1(X;Z) = 0</math> and using the [[Alexander duality|Alexander duality theorem]] on <math>S^2-X</math>, <math>\varinjlim\{H^q(U;\mathbb Z)\} = \mathbb Z</math> as <math>U</math> varies over neighborhoods of <math>X</math>.

Therefore, <math>\varinjlim\{H^q(U;\mathbb Z)\}\to H^1(X;\mathbb Z)</math> is not a [[monomorphism]] so that <math>X</math> is not a taut subspace of <math>\mathbb R^2</math> with respect to singular cohomology. However, since <math>X</math> is closed in <math>\mathbb R^2</math>, it's taut subspace with respect to Alexander cohomology.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Spanier |first1=Edwin H. |title=Tautness for Alexander-Spanier cohomology |journal=Pacific Journal of Mathematics |date=1978 |volume=75 |issue=2 |page=562|doi=10.2140/pjm.1978.75.561 |s2cid=122337937 |doi-access=free |url=https://projecteuclid.org/journals/pacific-journal-of-mathematics/volume-75/issue-2/Tautness-for-Alexander-Spanier-cohomology/pjm/1103121485.pdf }}</ref>
